markdown_report:
## Insights and directions

The starting evidence suggests three priorities. First, Electronics has 14.95% sampled wrong rankings and a −0.4812 tenth-percentile margin: improving difficult candidate discrimination deserves attention. These training diagnostics do not establish HR@10. Second, users report stale-history influence and weakly supported broad matches; recent behavioral evidence should influence ranking explicitly. Third, embedding similarity scores near 0.54 do not establish severe collapse, so diversity regularization lacks a strong diagnostic basis.

Three literature connections guide feasible directions. [gSASRec](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf) motivates learning against multiple negatives, although its calibrated BCE results do not establish sampled-softmax gains here. [LSIDN](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.14743) motivates separating persistent and transient interests, while warning that both contain noise. [GLSRec](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.datak.2026.102606) motivates directed behavioral transitions; observed transitions cannot establish equipment compatibility or complementarity.

## Framework and candidate ideas

| Direction | Evidence represented | Candidate | Main limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Objective | Candidate discrimination | A: uniform multi-negative softmax | Does not explicitly address stale intent |
| Temporal routing | Recent versus historical support | B: gated recent-support residual | Recency can overemphasize isolated purchases |
| Behavioral structure | Directed item transitions | C: sparse transition residual | Sparse edges and popularity confounding |

Scores below are prospective judgments, not experimental results. O=originality, P=potential, U=user alignment, M=model alignment; D=difficulty, with larger D meaning harder.

| Idea | O | P | U | M | D |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A | 3 | 7 | 4 | 9 | 3 |
| B | 4 | 8 | 8 | 8 | 4 |
| C | 5 | 7 | 7 | 6 | 5 |

A offers inexpensive discrimination improvements but leaves temporal failures untreated. B directly targets stale evidence and broad, weakly supported matches, but cannot infer practical compatibility. C captures asymmetric behavioral support but cannot label transitions as complements.

## Selected idea: gated recent-support residual

At 0% progress, choose B. Retain SASRec and add a small scoring branch that pools the last five visible item embeddings using learned exponential decay. A bounded gate combines this recent representation with SASRec’s state. Train the resulting scorer with 32 uniform negatives per position and sampled softmax.

This explicitly targets two user failures: older isolated interactions dominating current demand, and broad matches outranking candidates supported by recent specific behavior. Multiple competing negatives target the observed lower-tail ranking confusion. These are hypotheses requiring validation; semantic specificity and satisfied durable needs remain unresolved.

```text
h = SASRec(prefix)
r = decay_pool(last_five(prefix))
g = sigmoid(MLP(concat(h, r, h * r)))
score(j) = dot(h + g * r, item_embedding[j])
loss = cross_entropy(scores(positive + 32 negatives), positive_index)
```

Exclude padding and known training positives from negatives. Construct every prefix causally. Compare baseline, objective-only, and full variants using pinned macro validation HR@10 and record GPU cost. Preserve all four routes, seeds, diagnostic interfaces, and identical trained scoring in the predictor writer.

idea.description: Add a bounded, learned recent-history residual to SASRec scoring and train with uniform multi-negative sampled softmax. The residual uses the last five visible interactions and learned exponential decay; the gate conditions on the SASRec state, recent representation, and their elementwise interaction.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies stale or isolated historical evidence and broad, weakly supported matches as distinct ranking failures. Explicit recent support addresses both as testable hypotheses. Multi-negative training addresses observed candidate confusion, especially Electronics' 14.95% sampled wrong-ranking rate. Neither mechanism establishes compatibility, replacement demand, or actual user acceptance.
idea.implementation_notes: Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, four independently routed categories, and the SASREC_EPOCHS environment default of 200. Write checkpoints and generated predictor files beneath the trial directory. Use prefix-causal pooling at every supervised position; a candidate gate must never see the next item. Initialize the residual gate conservatively, such as bias -2, to keep initial scores close to SASRec. Sample 32 unique uniform negatives where the eligible catalog permits, excluding padding, the target, and all known training positives; use fewer when necessary. Do not inspect held-out interactions for filtering. Score negatives in chunks if memory requires it and keep execution single-GPU. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Expose the actual model through view.model and ensure log2feats and predict_score represent the gated scorer used at inference. Preserve existing measured margin definitions; report unavailable category breakdowns as unavailable rather than inventing metadata. Update the predictor writer to reconstruct and load the gate, pooling parameters, and trained embeddings. Compare baseline, objective-only, and full variants within the shared GPU budget; select only by pinned macro validation HR@10. No improvement has yet been measured.
idea.pseudocode:
For each category, retain the baseline training split and routing.
For each batch (None, sequence, positive, negative):
  h = SASRec.log2feats(sequence)
  r = prefix_causal_decay_pool(item_embeddings(sequence), window=5)
  g = sigmoid(MLP(concat(h, r, h * r)))
  features = h + g * r
  candidates = positive plus up to 32 eligible uniform negatives per valid position
  logits = dot(features, item_embeddings(candidates))
  loss = mean(cross_entropy(logits, positive_index=0))
  update all model parameters
Evaluate authorized validation candidates using identical scoring.
Generate working/predict.py with the same architecture and category routing.
Run diagnostics using the actual gated scoring model.

originality.positive: Connects explicit recent behavioral support with multi-candidate discrimination in a small SASRec extension tailored to the supplied diagnoses.
originality.negative: Gated temporal fusion and multi-negative objectives are established techniques; their combination is incremental.

future_potential.positive: Provides a low-cost foundation for testing whether temporal support explains ranking gains before introducing text encoders or transition graphs.
future_potential.negative: Recent interactions can themselves be misleading, and behavioral support cannot resolve unobserved practical requirements.

code_difficulty.positive: Adds a small pooling module and gate while retaining the existing item vocabulary, sequence encoder, and dataset routes.
code_difficulty.negative: Requires careful prefix masking, efficient negative filtering, and synchronized inference and diagnostic scoring.

related_work.title: SASRec
contributions: Uses causal self-attention over interaction histories for next-item recommendation.
limitations: The supplied diagnosis reports weak recent-intent specificity and dataset-dependent ranking confusion for the current implementation.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: The supplied search summary describes multiple-negative training with calibrated generalized BCE to address sampling-induced overconfidence.
limitations: Its reported objective differs from the proposed sampled softmax.
Its results do not establish gains on this pinned four-category evaluation.

related_work.title: LSIDN
contributions: The supplied search summary describes separate long- and short-term interest encoders with tailored denoising.
limitations: It motivates temporal separation but does not validate the proposed five-interaction residual.
Both recent and historical behavior may contain noise.

related_work.title: GLSRec
contributions: The supplied search summary describes combining directed global item-transition propagation with local sequence modeling.
limitations: Directed transitions do not establish factual complementarity or compatibility.
Graph construction and propagation add complexity relative to the selected initial experiment.
